questions.question: How did JPMorgan Chase's net income change from 2024 to 2025, and what was the primary driver of the difference?
questions.ground_truth_answer: JPMorgan Chase's net income declined from $58,471 million in 2024 to $57,048 million in 2025, a decrease of approximately $1,423 million (-2.4%). The primary driver was that 2024 net income was inflated by a $5.4 billion one-time gain related to Visa shares (from a $7.9B gross revenue gain, partially offset by a $1.0B contribution to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation). On a normalized basis, excluding the Visa gain, 2024 net income was approximately $53 billion, making 2025 core profitability actually stronger by approximately $4 billion.
questions.notes: Requires combining the Financial Highlights table (p. 2 & p. 76) with the 20-year earnings visual chart commentary (p. 8) which quantifies the normalized $5.4B Visa gain impact.

questions.question: How has JPMorgan Chase's diluted EPS grown from 2005 to 2025? Calculate the 20-year CAGR and decompose how much growth came from earnings expansion versus share count reduction.

20-Year CAGR Calculation: From $4.03 (2005) to $20.02 (2025) over 20 years: CAGR = (20.02/4.03)^(1/20) - 1 = (4.97)^(0.05) - 1 ≈ 8.2% annual EPS growth.

In recent years (2024→2025), shares fell from ~2,798M to ~2,696M (-3.6%), with buybacks meaningfully contributing to EPS growth.

Conclusion: The long-term EPS growth is primarily driven by earnings expansion (net income 6.7x) rather than buybacks, with buybacks becoming a more significant accelerant in the 2020s. The ~8.2% 20-year EPS CAGR places JPM among the strongest large-cap earnings compounders globally.

questions.question: What is the significance of JPMorgan Chase's CET1 capital ratio trend from 2005 to 2025, and what does the transition to Advanced risk-based ratios being 'more binding' mean for the firm's future capital strategy?
questions.ground_truth_answer:
CET1 Historical Trend (page 13 chart): Pre-Basel III (2005-2012): Ratios ranged ~7.0% to ~10.9%. Post-Basel III (2013+): Rose to 10.2%, 11.6%, then 12.0-12.9% range. COVID and beyond (2020-2022): 13.1%-15.6%. 2023-2024: 15.0%-15.7% (peak). 2025: Declined to 14.6% (partly Apple Card -25bps).

What 'Advanced Ratios Becoming More Binding' Means: Banks calculate capital under two approaches: Standardized (simpler, standard risk weights) and Advanced (internal models with potentially higher RWA). Advanced becoming binding means the firm's internal model-based capital requirement now exceeds the Standardized requirement, constraining capital planning to the tighter Advanced framework. This may: (1) limit future buybacks before hitting regulatory minima; (2) require higher buffers if Basel III Endgame tightens model weights; (3) reduce apparent excess capital vs. Standardized.

Long-Term Investor Significance: The trend from ~7% (2005) to 14.6% (2025) reflects massive capital accumulation that simultaneously funded 6.7x earnings growth. The fortress capital provides a buffer against future crises. The Advanced ratio transition introduces potential constraint on capital return velocity.

questions.question: How resilient has JPMorgan Chase's earnings been during the three major crises of the past 20 years (2008 GFC, 2020 COVID-19, 2022-2023 regional banking crisis), and what structural advantages enabled consistent profitability?
questions.ground_truth_answer:
2008 Global Financial Crisis: Reported net income $11.7B (significant but positive when most peers reported massive losses). EPS $2.26; ROTCE 10%. JPM was one of the few large banks that remained profitable throughout the GFC. Key advantage: Fortress balance sheet, conservative underwriting.

2020 COVID-19 Pandemic: Large provision build led to elevated provisions. However, ROTCE excluding reserve adjustments was 19.3% in 2020 — extremely strong underlying profitability. JPM received flood of deposit inflows: deposits/assets jumped from $3,258B (2019) to $3,781B (2020) and $4,488B (2021) (flight-to-quality).

2022-2023 Regional Banking Crisis: While SVB and other regional banks collapsed, JPM's CET1 was 15%+. JPM acquired First Republic Bank in 2023, contributing to the dramatic $5,292B asset/deposit total in 2023 vs. $4,240B in 2022. JPM absorbed distressed assets that competitors shed.

Structural Advantages: (1) Diversification across CCB, CIB, AWM providing offsetting revenues. (2) Fortress balance sheet with CET1 consistently above regulatory minimums. (3) 'Too big to fail' status generating flight-to-quality deposit inflows during crises. (4) Global scale providing countercyclical revenue sources. (5) Disciplined risk management.
